audits.mathematicalReason: The four unit-area regions tile the square, so its side is 2. Since AE = AH and [AEH] = 1, AE = AH = √2. Extend EH to meet line BC at X below B. Triangle BEX is right isosceles with legs 2 - √2. Triangle XIF is also right isosceles, with equal legs XI = FI. Its area is [BFIE] + [BEX], so FI²/2 = 1 + (2 - √2)²/2. Thus FI² = 8 - 4√2. This validates the external-triangle route. The coordinate route can instead compute BFIE by shoelace and FI by point-to-line distance; it is a valid alternative, not an additional required method.

figureEvidence.fact: The specified triangle, two quadrilaterals, and pentagon partition the square without gaps. Along EH the order is H, J, I, E, and the right-angle marks identify FI and GJ as perpendicular to EH.

audits.mathematicalReason: Let the original dimensions be w and h centimeters. The original diagonal gives w² + h² = 64. The inner cutout vertices differ horizontally by w - 2 and vertically by h - 2, so (w - 2)² + (h - 2)² = 32. Expanding and subtracting yields w + h = 10. Hence 2wh = (w + h)² - (w² + h²) = 100 - 64 = 36, and the area is 18 cm². The dimensions are 5 ± √7, both greater than 2, consistent with the depicted cutouts. The Pythagorean, rectangle-area, and algebraic scopes are defensible.

figureEvidence.fact: The removed unit squares occupy opposite corners. The 4√2 segment joins their inward vertices, each inset 1 cm from both adjacent original sides; the segment labeled 8 joins the other pair of original opposite corners.

audits.mathematicalReason: The ratio AD:DC = 1:2 gives [ABD] = 120 and [DBC] = 240. Since E is the midpoint of BD, [ABE] = 60 and [EBC] = 120. Therefore A's altitude to BC is three times E's altitude to BC. If x = [EBF], the common base BF gives [ABF] = 3x, while the partition by BE gives [ABF] = 60 + x. Thus x = 30. This uses exactly median equal-area relations and the triangle-area formula. Alternatively, a parallel to BC through D and triangle similarity yield BF:FC = 1:3 and the same requested area.

figureEvidence.fact: The diagram shows A, D, C collinear; B, E, D collinear; A, E, F collinear; and F between B and C. Thus BE partitions triangle ABF into ABE and EBF.

audits.mathematicalReason: Using the axes as drawn, reflection across q sends (x, y) to (y, x), and subsequent reflection across horizontal p sends this to (y, -x). The composition is a 90° clockwise rotation about their intersection. Consequently the M moves to the lower-right region, with its original top pointing right. Slot 9 has both the correct location and orientation. Tracking reflected key points is sufficient, so the proposed reflection-drawing and reflection-property scopes are appropriate without requiring a separate rotation method.

figureEvidence.fact: Line p is horizontal, q is the rising 45° diagonal as drawn, and the upright M is above p, to the right of the vertical reference line, and above q.
Choice A places the letter in the lower-right region but gives the opposite sideways orientation from the required clockwise-rotated M.

audits.mathematicalReason: A nonzero translation by one complete repeating period preserves the pattern. A half-turn about a point on ℓ where an upper square's right edge meets a lower square's left edge also preserves both the squares and their diagonal attachments. Reflection across ℓ fails because upper and lower squares occupy alternating horizontal intervals. Reflection across any perpendicular line reverses the slope of every short diagonal, producing attachments absent from the pattern. Therefore exactly the rotation and translation categories work. Central symmetry, translation, and line symmetry are the appropriate assessed concepts.

figureEvidence.fact: Equal squares alternate above and below ℓ. Upper squares have outward attachments at their upper-right corners, and lower squares at their lower-left corners; all short diagonals have the same rising slope. The motif repeats along ℓ.

audits.derivedAnswer: B: m + n + p = -4, since the area is 16√3 - 23.
audits.mathematicalReason: Write r = √3. A unit regular hexagon has distance r between opposite parallel sides. In the overlapping arrangement shown, the enclosing square consequently has side 2r - 1. Consider an inward junction between the top and right hexagons. By diagonal symmetry it lies u beyond each corresponding side of the central square. The 30°-60°-90° edge triangle gives r - 1 - u = ru, hence u = 2 - r. Each missing bounding-square corner splits into two triangles, each with base r - 1 and height r - 1 - u = 2r - 3. Its total area is (r - 1)(2r - 3) = 9 - 5r. Thus the polygon area is (2r - 1)² - 4(9 - 5r) = 16r - 23. Here m = 16, n = 3 is squarefree, and p = -23, giving -4. This validates the proposed enclosing-square decomposition and its supporting angle and right-triangle procedures.

figureEvidence.fact: The hexagons overlap rather than forming four disjoint outward attachments: the topmost hexagon shares the central square's bottom edge, and the analogous arrangement occurs on the other sides.

The bold outer boundary has four extreme horizontal or vertical sides and four inward junctions, each joined to the neighboring extreme sides by two slanted segments. Each omitted corner of an enclosing square is therefore split into two triangles.

audits.mathematicalReason: Let the side lengths of S1, S2, and S3 be a, b, and c. The horizontal arrangement gives a + b + c = 3322. The vertical alignments give a + c - b = 2020. Subtracting yields 2b = 1302, so b = 651. This uses equal sides of squares and addition/subtraction of aligned segments, matching the proposed scopes. No equality between the side lengths of S1 and S3 is assumed from their similar appearance.

figureEvidence.fact: Horizontally the three square widths contribute consecutively to the outer width. The bottoms of S1 and S2 align with the top of R1, while the tops of S2 and S3 align with the bottom of R2. S1 reaches the outer top and S3 reaches the outer bottom.

audits.mathematicalReason: Let P be the medians' intersection. The centroid divides each median 2:1 from its vertex, so MP = CP = 8. Since the medians are perpendicular, [MPC] = 8·8/2 = 32. Triangle MPC has one-third the area of AMC, giving [AMC] = 96. The alternative route is also valid: quadrilateral UVCM has perpendicular diagonals of length 12, so its area, obtained by summing four right triangles, is 72. Since U and V are midpoints, triangle AUV is similar to AMC with scale factor 1/2 and has one-quarter its area. Hence 72 is three-quarters of the requested area, again giving 96.

figureEvidence.fact: The entire medians MV and CU are labeled 12 and cross at P with a right-angle mark. U lies on AM and V lies on AC, so MV and CU are also the diagonals of quadrilateral UVCM.
